title: Guiding to good
hookLine: whoever guides to good gets a reward like the one who does it
tomorrow: a kid asks Amira something she can't answer. now what?

cards: A friend asks where to donate a winter coat. You don't have one to give, so you send her the shelter's address. She drops it off.
Whose good deed is that? In Sahih Muslim, a man comes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with exactly that kind of gap.

teach.h: I HAVE NONE TO GIVE YOU.
teach.b: His riding animal is gone, and he's stuck far from home. He asks the Prophet for a mount. The Prophet says: I have none to give you.

teach.h: I CAN POINT HIM TO SOMEONE.
teach.b: Then another man speaks up: Messenger of God, I can point him to someone who will.
And the Prophet says: whoever guides to good gets a reward like the one who does it. Like the doer. Not a smaller cut for being the middleman.
Not a thank-you note. A reward like it, for the one who only knew where to look. The word for reward is ajr, a wage.
In the hadith's math, the one who sent the address and the one who gave the coat are both paid for the coat. Now look back at the week. Convey even one verse: pointing.
Learn and teach: pointing. Gently, and by example: pointing with your whole life.

teach.h: THE SIGNPOST IS PAID IN FULL.
teach.b: Every teacher this week was a kind of signpost, and the hadith says the signpost is paid in full.
One to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, pointing someone to the good is counted like doing it.

how: Muslims quote this hadith when they share a good cause, a class or a charity with others, counting the referral itself as part of the good deed.

o: pointing someone toward a good deed
giving advice only when you're asked
leading the prayer at the mosque

games.q: the week's lines — tap the pairs.

s: the one who points someone to a good deed gets a smaller share of the reward
the hadith says a reward like the one who does it.
in the story, the Prophet himself had no riding animal to give
'I have none to give you.' another man pointed the way.
guiding to good only counts when you're teaching religion
the man in the story pointed a stranded traveler to someone with a mount.

games.q: a classmate is stuck on a scholarship essay. essays aren't your thing, but your roommate edits them for fun. what does today's hadith point to?
o: connect them; whoever guides to good gets the doer's reward.
try to edit it yourself, since only the doer gets rewarded.
stay out of it; it isn't your skill, so it isn't your job.
games.why: the Prophet had no mount to give, and a man pointed the way instead. whoever guides to good gets a reward like the one who does it.

practice: Bring to mind one person looking for something good: a job lead, a class, a doctor, a place to volunteer. Write them the message that points the way, a name, a link, an address, and keep it ready to send.

wordCard.voice: Guiding to good: pointing someone toward a good deed. In the hadith, the one who points gets the doer's reward.

orig.note: Arabic: 'whoever guides to good', the hadith's opening words.

carryVoice: One to keep: the reward of the doer, even when your part was only pointing. Two weeks, carried.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 1893 (Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari): a man whose mount had perished asks for one; 'I have none'; another man offers to point him to someone who will; whoever guides to good has a reward like the one who does it
